subject: Egypt
note: Hand-curated research for a Geographica episode about Bir Tawil. Claims are cited to a pinned Wikipedia revision (trusted_secondary). Bir Tawil is not an entity in the map data, so it is a labelled approximate point on the Egypt–Sudan border. The Halaib Triangle, claimed by both countries, is not drawn or labelled. Needs the disputed-borders sign-off before release (Sudan has a flagged area, Abyei, which this episode does not show).

claims.text: Bir Tawil is a 2,060 km² area of land along the border between Egypt and Sudan which is claimed by neither country.
Its unclaimed status results from a discrepancy between the straight political boundary between Egypt and Sudan established in 1899 and the irregular administrative boundary established in 1902.
Egypt asserts the political boundary, and Sudan asserts the administrative boundary, so the Halaib Triangle is claimed by both and Bir Tawil by neither.

bir-tawil.note: The centre of Bir Tawil, on the Egypt–Sudan border, to the nearest tenth of a degree.
